🚨 TRAFFIC ADVISORY 🚨

In view of the ongoing construction works at Novopan Junction on NH-65, traffic diversions will be in force from 24.05.2026 until completion of the work.

Commuters travelling towards Patancheru and Sangareddy are requested to follow the designated diversion routes and plan their journey accordingly to avoid inconvenience.

We request citizens to cooperate with Cyberabad Traffic Police and follow traffic advisories for smooth and safe vehicular movement.

data.raw_text:
This little boy saved up for months. What he did with $3 will break you open.
His name is Miko. He's 8 years old, lives in Cebu, Philippines, and every time his lola gave him five pesos for being good  he didn't spend it.

He hid it inside a folded piece of paper tucked under his mattress. Coin by coin. Week by week. He told no one what it was for.

His grandfather  Lolo Carding, 79 years old  hadn't eaten at a restaurant in over a decade. Not since Lola passed. "Wala nang saysay," he would say quietly. No point anymore.

One Saturday morning, Miko walked into his lolo's room, held out a small crumpled envelope, and said: "Lolo, I saved enough. I want to take you out to eat."

Inside the envelope: 170 pesos. Just over $3.

He had already chosen the place  a Korean barbecue restaurant two jeepney rides away that he'd seen his classmates talk about. He didn't know if $3 was enough. He just knew his lolo deserved a table with a fire in the middle of it.

The owner seated them at the best spot by the window. When he understood what was happening  this tiny boy, this old man, this crumpled envelope he quietly told the staff: cook everything, charge nothing extra.

Miko carefully placed every peso on the table himself. He wanted to pay. He needed to pay.

Lolo Carding didn't say much. He just watched his grandson pile meat onto his plate, blow on each piece so it wouldn't be too hot, and beam across the table like he'd just given him the whole world.

Because he had.

When someone later asked Miko why he saved so long for this, he shrugged and said: "Lolo always eats alone. I don't want him to eat alone."

Three dollars. Two plates of Korean barbecue. One little boy who understood something about love that most adults have forgotten.
 In your life, you shouldn't be eating alone !

hi bloomtwt and zaiatwt, a friend of a friend reached out to us regarding the fire that broke out in parola, binondo, manila. they are asking for help because the only things they were able to save from the fire were their important documents. other than that, everything was destroyed.

if you are nearby and have the means to donate clothes or other necessities, please consider reaching out to them. you may also retweet this post to help it reach more people who might be willing to help.
thank you!

on the third and fourth pic po ay yung ss ng convo nung person na need ng help.

you can directly message the person through her fb account:

Danica V Matados
